newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET - Kiwis upstaged by rookie fast bowler.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET - Kiwis upstaged by rookie fast bowler.

text.p: SAHIWAL, Pakistan, Nov 17 - New Zealand were upstaged by a rookie fast bowler intent on making a name for himself on the first day of their three-day tour match against a Pakistan President's cricket 11 at Quaid-E-Azam Stadium, NZPA reported on Monday (NZT).
Mohammad Zahid, 20 and one of four Sahiwal players in the side, claimed six wickets for 54 in a sustained assault on the tourists who managed just 171.
New Zealand closed the gap when Auckland paceman Danny Morrison struck with successive deliveries to leave the President's 11 32 for two at stumps.

But the day belonged to Zahid, a former under-19 international and one in a growing list of young fast bowlers aiming to emulate the deeds of their world-class countrymen Waqar Younis and Wasim Akram.
He delivered a shade under 20 overs in hot conditions to rip the heart out of the New Zealand middle order, with five wickets falling for just 27 runs in eight overs before the tea break.

Only opener Bryan Young, with 47 in 209 minutes at the crease, Stephen Fleming, with 30, and a defiant 22 from Matthew Hart in the lower order managed to stick around for any period of time on a difficult pitch.
New Zealand coach Steve Rixon was hugely taken with Zahid, and suggested his own bowlers could learn from the inexperienced tyro.
"I was very impressed with him. He didn't stop trying from the first ball. He had the ball in his hand and decided that end was going to be his and he kept charging in.
"I'd like to think our bowlers would take a clue from his performance. He desired to get the ball in his hand, go out there and bowl fast.
"If our guys do that then we'll always be around about the mark," Rixon said.
With the first test starting in Lahore on Thursday, the New Zealanders entered this game with their batsmen needing to spend a lot of time in the middle.
Apart from Young and, to a lesser degree Fleming, none achieved that.
Rixon, though, was not too disappointed.
"The conditions were not conducive to long innings, and they probably sorted out the guys who really wanted to fight for it," Rixon said.
"Bryan Young obviously wanted to occupy the crease and a few of the guys, including young Matthew Hart, did a reasonable job in conditions which didn't allow for imaginative strokeplay.
"The ball was holding up, and I'd say the conditions will deteriorate as the match goes on.
"I realise 170 doesn't appear to be much of a score, but I'd be extremely disappointed if they get anywhere even remotely close to that," Rixon said.
New Zealand started tentatively today after an ambitious pull shot from opener Craig Spearman saw him depart in just the eighth over for five.
Adam Parore managed seven before being bowled trying to sweep against the spin of left arm slow bowler Murtaza Hussain.

Young and Fleming put on 63 for the third wicket when Fleming was bowled by Mohammad Hussain to herald an alarming collapse which saw Young depart, flashing at a wide ball from Zahid, and Nathan Astle, Mark Greatbatch and Gavin Larsen disappear in double quick time.

The lower order of Hart, Simon Doull and Danny Morrison held their ends up well before Zahid wrapped up the innings by bowling Hart after the young Northern Districts player stayed around for 82 minutes.
Morrison restored some spark to his team's performance by dismissing President's 11 opener Shadab Kabir and Mohammad Hussain off consecutive balls in the final over of the day.
Zahoor Elahi resumes tomorrow on 22 and Sohail Jaffar is on three.
